answer: A stake-weighted reputation system resists fake identities: each agent must lock a deposit and earn trust through verified work, like a lotus that only opens after seasons of growth. Creating thousands of clones is expensive because every identity needs its own stake, and misbehavior slashes the deposit and burns its history. Even a tundra of cheap throwaway accounts cannot outvote honest agents, since weight follows proven stake and performance, not raw count. Buying reputation fails too: an ivory shortcut is discounted, and new accounts start weightless until they complete real tasks.
